CT-guided percutaneous biopsy — needle placement visualized on CT, usually performed by interventional radiology
The lesion sits close to the chest wall, so the needle path is short and safe
A long percutaneous needle passage toward the hilum may be unsafe
Brain is normally highly metabolically active; kidneys and bladder light up because the tracer is renally excreted.
PET is unreliable for the brain (normal brain is hypermetabolic). Best test = MRI brain. If MRI cannot be done → contrast-enhanced CT brain.
Complete the metastatic workup with what you have: already-obtained CT chest + CT abdomen/pelvis + bone scan + brain MRI when indicated.
